papers.title: Ferroptosis-related endothelial protection by Danhong injection in cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion injury: network pharmacology and validation in endothelial cells.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke and ischemic acute kidney injury are both clinical challenges. Danhong injection (DHI) has been reported to exert protective effects against cerebral and renal ischemic injury. However, the shared therapeutic targets and mechanisms underlying its effects in these two organs remain unclear. Using network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and in vitro experiments, this study investigated shared targets and pathways associated with cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and evaluated whether DHI exerted a shared ferroptosis-related endot
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology, molecular docking, and endothelial cell experiments to identify shared therapeutic targets of Danhong injection in both cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion injury. The authors propose that DHI protects endothelial cells through ferroptosis-related mechanisms common to both organs. The work is largely computational with limited in vitro validation.

papers.title: Efficient flavonoids from Helichrysum bracteatum and their multi-target antioxidant mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Helichrysum bracteatum is a promising source of natural antioxidants for food preservation. However, unclear mechanisms and inefficient extraction limit the application of its flavonoids in functional foods. Here, we report a response surface methodology (RSM)-optimized hydroethanolic reflux extraction yielding a maximum flavonoid extraction yield of 16.0% under optimized conditions (27: 1 mL/g, 68% ethanol, 1.6 h). The major flavonoids identified were quercetin (29.44%), kaempferol (8.03%), and rutin (3.44%), and the extract exhibited strong radical-scavenging activity. Network analysis ident
papers.summary: This study optimized flavonoid extraction from Helichrysum bracteatum using response surface methodology, achieving a 16.0% yield under optimized hydroethanolic reflux conditions. The main flavonoids identified were quercetin, kaempferol, and rutin, and the extract showed strong radical-scavenging activity. Network analysis was used to explore the multi-target antioxidant mechanisms underlying these effects.

papers.title: Membrane lipid-driven gating of TREK-1 channels: Revisiting anesthetic mechanisms beyond protein targets.
papers.abstract: The mechanistic basis of general anesthesia has long been debated between protein-centric and lipid-centric frameworks, and the TWIK-related potassium channel 1 (TREK-1), a member of the two-pore domain K+ (K2P) superfamily, sits at the intersection of the two as a physiologically relevant target of both volatile and intravenous anesthetics. Although the direct interaction of anesthetics with TREK-1 protein has been studied extensively, how membrane lipid composition and lipid-driven conformational dynamics modulate channel gating remains insufficiently explored. In this review, we synthesize
papers.summary: This review examines how membrane lipid composition and lipid-driven conformational dynamics gate TREK-1 potassium channels, arguing that anesthetic mechanisms extend beyond direct protein binding to include lipid-mediated effects. It synthesizes evidence positioning TREK-1 at the intersection of protein-centric and lipid-centric frameworks for general anesthesia.

papers.title: Network pharmacology and molecular dynamics uncover RMJ's targets and mechanisms for treating atherosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerosis involves complex pathogenesis including inflammation, lipid disorders, and abnormal autophagy, yet current treatments are limited by adverse reactions and drug resistance, highlighting the need for novel strategies.
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology combined with molecular dynamics simulations to identify the protein targets and mechanisms through which RMJ (a compound or formula) may treat atherosclerosis. The approach maps RMJ's interactions onto inflammation, lipid, and autophagy pathways implicated in the disease. The work is computational and predictive, offering candidate targets and mechanistic hypotheses rather than experimental validation.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Natural Product Pharmacology: From Molecular Discovery to Precision Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: The use of natural products as a chemically diverse source of bioactive molecules for drug development has been well established; however, their multicomponent and multitarget nature, uncertain target causality, variable in vivo exposure, and heterogeneous responses to therapy make them challenging to characterize pharmacologically and translate into clinical practice. Systems pharmacology, together with artificial intelligence (AI), provides new approaches for molecular screening, target prioritization, integration of multidimensional data, and development of precision therapeutics. Osteoarth
papers.summary: This review discusses how artificial intelligence combined with systems pharmacology can address the challenges of natural product drug development, including their multicomponent nature, uncertain target causality, and variable in vivo exposure. The authors describe AI-driven approaches for molecular screening, target prioritization, multidimensional data integration, and precision therapeutic development, using osteoarthritis as a case example.

papers.title: GNG2-MRAS interaction regulates SHOC2-dependent RAF activation and MAPK signaling.
papers.abstract: Dysregulation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway is a hallmark of many human cancers and RASopathies. The SHOC2-MRAS-PP1Cα (SMP) holophosphatase complex is a crucial regulatory node of this pathway. It activates the MAPK pathway by dephosphorylating the inhibitory phosphoserine on RAF kinases and thereby relieving RAF autoinhibition. Although GNG2, the γ-subunit of heterotrimeric G proteins, has recently emerged as a negative modulator of MAPK signaling, its molecular mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify GNG2 and its truncated var
papers.summary: This study identifies GNG2, the gamma subunit of heterotrimeric G proteins, as a negative regulator of MAPK signaling that acts by interacting with MRAS and disrupting the SHOC2-MRAS-PP1Cα holophosphatase complex, which normally dephosphorylates and activates RAF kinases. The authors also characterize a truncated GNG2 variant, revealing a molecular mechanism by which GNG2 restrains RAF activation and MAPK pathway output. This clarifies how a G-protein subunit feeds into the RAS-RAF-MAPK axis, with implications for cancers and RASopathies driven by pathway dysregulation.

papers.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine-Derived Natural Products: Potential Effects on Mitochondrial Energy Metabolism in Heart Failure.
papers.abstract: Heart failure (HF), the end-stage of cardiovascular disease (CVD), affects over 64 million people globally. There is an alarming trend of earlier onset, which poses a substantial healthcare burden. Although guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) has significantly improved clinical outcomes, residual morbidity and mortality remain considerable, highlighting the need for additional therapeutic strategies. Mitochondrial energy metabolism (MEM) plays an important role in HF pathophysiology and represents a potential therapeutic target. Traditional Chinese Medicine-derived natural products (TCM-
papers.summary: This review examines how natural products derived from Traditional Chinese Medicine may influence mitochondrial energy metabolism in heart failure. It argues that mitochondrial dysfunction is a key driver of heart failure pathophysiology and a promising therapeutic target, and surveys TCM-derived compounds with potential effects on these pathways. The abstract is truncated, so specific compounds and mechanistic findings are not detailed.

papers.title: GO- and calcium silicate NP-modified diamides for enhanced antimicrobial activity: structural, morphological, and in silico investigations.
papers.abstract: We herein report the preparation and investigation of antimicrobial nanohybrid systems based on antimicrobial diamides and GO, as well as CaSiO3 NPs. Diamides were synthesized by condensation of 4-nitrobenzoyl chloride with aromatic diamines under catalyst-free conditions, followed by non-covalent conjugation of the obtained compounds with GO and CaSiO3. Synthesized diamides, NPs, and nanoensembles were investigated by spectroscopic, microscopic, and diffraction techniques. The obtained two-component nanohybrid systems were examined against bacterial and yeast strains, which demonstrated their
papers.summary: This study synthesized new diamide compounds and combined them non-covalently with graphene oxide and calcium silicate nanoparticles to create antimicrobial nanohybrid systems. The resulting two-component nanohybrids were tested against bacterial and yeast strains and showed enhanced antimicrobial activity, with structural and morphological characterization plus computational (in silico) analysis supporting the findings.

papers.title: Pyrazolyl-triazolyl chalcones as promising antimycobacterial candidates: integrating experimental and computational insights.
papers.abstract: In pursuit of developing novel antitubercular scaffolds, a series of pyrazolyl-triazolyl-functionalized chalcones (6a-o) were synthesized and evaluated for their antimycobacterial activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis H37Rv using the MABA assay. The synthesized compounds exhibited promising inhibitory potential, with minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values ranging from 1.6 to 12.5 µg mL-1. Among them, compounds 6b and 6k emerged as the most potent analogues (MIC = 1.6 µg mL-1), followed by compounds 6c, 6d, 6g, 6h, 6j, and 6l displaying strong activity (MIC = 3.12 µg mL-1). Molecul
papers.summary: This study synthesized a series of pyrazolyl-triazolyl chalcone derivatives and tested them against Mycobacterium tuberculosis, finding several compounds with promising antimycobacterial activity (MIC as low as 1.6 µg/mL). The most potent compounds were further analyzed using computational methods to understand their binding interactions, supporting their potential as new anti-tuberculosis drug candidates.

papers.title: Water-network reorganization upon ligand binding in BRD4 bromodomains: An integrated hydration-site analysis.
papers.abstract: Water molecules play critical roles in ligand binding to BRD4 bromodomains (BD1 and BD2). Although crystallographic studies have provided extensive structural information on these water molecules, how water-mediated interactions reorganize under different ligand-binding conditions remains poorly understood. Here, we performed an integrated characterization of hydration sites based on crystal structures and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate water-mediated interactions and network reorganizations associated with ligand binding. Systematic spatial clustering of crystallographic w
papers.summary: This study integrates crystallographic data and molecular dynamics simulations to map hydration sites in the BRD4 bromodomains BD1 and BD2, revealing how water-mediated interaction networks reorganize upon ligand binding. The work provides a systematic characterization of conserved versus ligand-dependent water networks, offering structural insight that could inform drug design targeting bromodomains.

papers.title: Integrating artificial intelligence prescreening with molecular dynamics for the design of peptide-based WWP1 inhibitors as promising therapeutic agents against breast cancer, including the triple-negative subtype.
papers.abstract: Breast cancer (BC) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related death in women. BC is classified into three primary subtypes, of which triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) carries the poorest prognosis because it lacks specific targetable markers. Preclinical studies of TNBC have consistently reported reduced tumor-suppressor activity of PTEN, activating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. Notably, published studies have shown that the WWP1 enzyme plays a pivotal role in driving PTEN degradation via ubiquitination, identifying it as a promising therap
papers.summary: This study uses AI-based prescreening combined with molecular dynamics simulations to design peptide inhibitors targeting the WWP1 enzyme, which drives PTEN degradation and activates oncogenic PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling in breast cancer, particularly triple-negative breast cancer. The work identifies candidate peptide inhibitors as potential therapeutic agents for a subtype with few targeted treatment options.

papers.title: Molecular Dynamics Insight into Softening Mechanism of Zirconia and Prediction of Removal Depth in Magnetic Abrasive Finishing.
papers.abstract: Zirconia ceramic is widely used in dentistry and precision industries owing to its high hardness and fracture toughness. Nevertheless, its high hardness and toughness cause severe tool wear, and microcracks tend to form on the machined surface during conventional mechanical processing. This paper proposes a NaOH-PVP-deionized water composite system to realize green chemical softening of zirconia at room temperature and atmospheric pressure. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that OH- forms strong chemical bonds with surface Zr atoms, thereby inducing surface hydroxylation and increasing the
papers.summary: This paper proposes a NaOH-PVP-water composite system for chemically softening zirconia ceramic at room temperature and pressure, aiming to reduce tool wear and microcracks during machining. Molecular dynamics simulations show that hydroxide ions bond strongly with surface zirconium atoms, inducing surface hydroxylation and softening the material, and the work further predicts removal depth for magnetic abrasive finishing. The study is a materials-processing contribution combining simulation with a green chemical approach rather than a biological or biomedical finding.

papers.title: Computational and Experimental Studies of PSMA-Targeted Conjugates Designed for Subcellular Delivery of Theranostic Radiometals to Prostate Cancer Cells.
papers.abstract: Background: The membrane receptor prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a validated target for theranostic radioconjugates in the treatment and imaging of prostate cancer (PCa). Radioconjugates targeted at PSMA rely mostly on the peptidomimetic glutamate-urea-lysine (Glu-urea-Lys) binding motif to facilitate tumor accumulation. The combination of this binding motif with subcellular targeting moieties, such as acridine orange (AO) and triphenylphosphonium (TPP) derivatives, for nuclear and mitochondrial delivery, respectively, might open the way to innovative dual-target approaches. This
papers.summary: This study computationally designs and experimentally tests PSMA-targeted radioconjugates that combine the Glu-urea-Lys binding motif with subcellular-targeting moieties (acridine orange for nuclear delivery and triphenylphosphonium for mitochondrial delivery) to deliver theranostic radiometals to prostate cancer cells. The work explores a dual-targeting strategy aimed at improving radioconjugate efficacy beyond simple tumor accumulation.

papers.title: Computational Structural and Dynamic Insights into the Proposed TcP21-CXCR4 Interaction: A Consensus-Based Multireplica Simulation Approach.
papers.abstract: Chagas disease, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi, is a neglected tropical disease with limited therapeutic options, underscoring the need for novel targeted strategies. The parasite's secreted 21 kDa virulence factor, TcP21, promotes extracellular amastigote host-cell invasion and persistence by interacting with the human chemokine receptor CXCR4, a class A G protein-coupled receptor. Despite its biological importance, the structural determinants governing TcP21-CXCR4 complex formation remain unknown. To elucidate the molecular basis of this host-parasite recognition, multiple initial candidate bin
papers.summary: This study uses consensus-based multireplica molecular dynamics simulations to model how the Trypanosoma cruzi virulence factor TcP21 binds to the human chemokine receptor CXCR4, a key step in Chagas disease host-cell invasion. The authors propose structural determinants of the TcP21-CXCR4 interface, offering a computational hypothesis for a host-parasite recognition event that has not been structurally characterized. The work is purely computational and provides a starting point for experimental validation of the interaction.

papers.title: Integrated Toxicological, Network Toxicology, and Molecular Simulation Assessment of Inhalation Toxicity and Mechanisms of HFO-1336mzz(E) as an SF6 Alternative Insulating Gas.
papers.abstract: HFO-1336mzz-(E) is a novel environmentally friendly insulating gas with a low global warming potential and favorable dielectric properties, and it has been regarded as an important potential substitute for sulfur hexafluoride (SF6). However, its systemic toxicological characteristics and underlying mechanisms under inhalation exposure remain insufficiently investigated. To address this issue, the present study, for the first time, systematically evaluated the biological safety of HFO-1336mzz-(E) by integrating multilevel toxicological assessment with molecular mechanistic analysis. Acute inhal
papers.summary: This study provides the first systematic safety assessment of HFO-1336mzz(E), an environmentally friendly insulating gas proposed as a replacement for SF6, using acute inhalation toxicology combined with network toxicology and molecular docking/simulation. The authors identify toxicological endpoints and propose molecular mechanisms of action for inhalation exposure, supporting the compound's biological safety profile as an SF6 alternative.

papers.title: Investigating Ferritin Permeability to Metal-Based Drugs through Molecular Dynamics.
papers.abstract: In this study, we implemented a workflow based on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to assess whether gold-(I)-containing complexes can traverse the C3 channels of human H ferritin and which energetic barriers were at play in the process. By using two example complexes for which an extensive experimental characterization was already available, we observed that classical MD correctly indicated which one could spontaneously pass through the channel. To quantify the ability of the ferritin nanocage to retain the internalized complex, we estimated, through steered MD and umbrella sampling simula
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to test whether gold-containing drug complexes can pass through the C3 channels of human H ferritin, a protein cage that could serve as a drug delivery vehicle. Classical MD correctly predicted which of two experimentally characterized complexes could spontaneously traverse the channel, and steered MD with umbrella sampling quantified the energetic barriers and the cage's ability to retain the internalized drug. The work provides a computational workflow for assessing ferritin permeability to metal-based therapeutics.

papers.title: Solving the Computational Peptide Design Puzzle: Challenges and Opportunities.
papers.abstract: Peptides are increasingly recognized as promising therapeutics, antimicrobial agents, and supramolecular biomaterials due to the remarkable versatility encoded in their amino acid sequences. However, the rational design of peptides remains challenging because sequence-structure-function relationships are not yet fully understood. Experimental exploration of peptide chemical space is inherently limited by the vast number of possible sequences and the complexity of resolving peptide behavior at molecular resolution. Computational methods, particularly molecular dynamics simulations and, more rec
papers.summary: This review discusses the challenges and opportunities in computational peptide design, emphasizing that sequence-structure-function relationships remain incompletely understood. It highlights molecular dynamics simulations and emerging computational approaches as key tools for navigating the vast peptide sequence space, which is too large for exhaustive experimental exploration.

papers.title: Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma species are the minimal-genome pathogens that elicit complex host immune responses involving both protective and pathogenic inflammation. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) are pivotal components of the immune system, recognizing pathogen-associated molecular patterns and damage-associated molecular patterns to initiate immune responses. TLRs recognize Mycoplasma-derived lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA motifs, initiating NF-κB and MAPK signaling cascades. While these pathways are indispensable for microbial clearance, their dysregulation contributes to chronic inflammation, auto
papers.summary: This review examines how Toll-like receptors recognize Mycoplasma components such as lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG-rich DNA, triggering NF-κB and MAPK signaling that can both clear infection and drive chronic inflammation. The authors integrate cheminformatics and machine learning approaches to identify and prioritize potential TLR-targeted therapeutic compounds. The work synthesizes immunopathogenesis with computational drug-discovery strategies for Mycoplasma infections.

papers.title: Structural Characterization of Mycobacterium tuberculosis IspQ Reveals Membrane-Dependent Stabilization of Its Conserved Electron-Transfer Cofactor Network.
papers.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis persistence in granulomas depends on lipid catabolism through the β-oxidation-coupled respiratory pathway, which requires the essential membrane-associated protein IspQ, encoded by Rv0338c. Although IspQ is a genetically and chemically validated drug target, its structural organization and membrane-dependent function remain unknown. Using AlphaFold3 structure prediction, cofactor mapping, evolutionary conservation analysis, and atomistic molecular dynamics simulations, we show that IspQ adopts an EtfD-like fold containing four iron-sulfur clusters, a heme b, and a me
papers.summary: The study uses AlphaFold3 structure prediction, cofactor mapping, and molecular dynamics simulations to characterize the Mycobacterium tuberculosis protein IspQ, showing it adopts an EtfD-like fold with four iron-sulfur clusters, a heme b cofactor, and a membrane-binding region. The findings indicate that IspQ's electron-transfer cofactor network is stabilized in a membrane-dependent manner, providing structural insight into a validated drug target for tuberculosis. This work lays groundwork for structure-based drug design against persistent M. tuberculosis infections.

papers.title: Theoretical Calculations of CO2/CH4 Separation through Windowed Carbon Nanotube Membranes.
papers.abstract: Distinct topological features endow windowed carbon nanotube (CNT) membranes with great potential as molecular sieves for efficient gas separation and purification. In this work, molecular dynamics (MD) simulations were adopted to systematically investigate the CO2/CH4 selective separation performance of such membranes. Key structural and operational parameters, including CNT diameter, pressure, initial feed gas molar ratio, and nanowindow density, were modulated to comprehensively evaluate the molecular sieving capacity toward CO2 and CH4. Simulation results reveal that heteroatom-functionali
papers.summary: This study uses molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate how windowed carbon nanotube membranes separate CO2 from CH4, systematically varying CNT diameter, pressure, feed gas ratio, and nanowindow density. The results show that heteroatom functionalization and structural parameters strongly influence molecular sieving performance, suggesting these membranes could be tuned for efficient gas separation and purification.

papers.title: Prospects of time-resolved vibrational electron energy loss spectroscopy: A FTE-TACAW method.
papers.abstract: Seeing that ultrafast (picosecond timescale) vibrational electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) should soon be experimentally realizable, we present an in silico approach capable of providing insight from the computational physics perspective. We present a framework that combines frozen trajectory excitation (FTE) with time auto-correlation of auxiliary wavefunctions (TACAW) to study the time-dependent spectral response of non-equilibrium lattice dynamics in a way comparable directly to experiment-(scanning) transmission electron microscope EELS, (S)TEM-EELS. In this approach, a selected pho
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework (FTE-TACAW) for simulating time-resolved vibrational electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) on picosecond timescales, combining frozen trajectory excitation with time autocorrelation of auxiliary wavefunctions. The method aims to predict the time-dependent spectral response of non-equilibrium lattice dynamics, enabling direct comparison with future ultrafast STEM-EELS experiments. It is a theoretical/methodological contribution rather than an experimental finding.

papers.title: CryoID2: deep learning-enhanced identification of protein and RNA from cryoEM maps.
papers.abstract: Identifying the molecular components of cryoEM/cryoET maps of endogenous or poorly characterized complexes remains a major bottleneck. CryoID2 addresses this by integrating deep learning-based feature prediction with sequence prioritization and structural evaluation. Three 3D U-Nets extract structure classes, key-atom positions, and reduced residue/nucleotide types from the input map. These predictions support backbone tracing and the generation of short sequence queries that rank candidates from a user-supplied pool-using BLASTp for proteins and a maximin strategy for RNA. Corresponding PDB o
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CryoID2 is a new computational tool that uses deep learning to identify proteins and RNA within cryoEM and cryoET density maps of unknown or poorly characterized complexes. Three 3D U-Nets predict structural features such as key-atom positions and reduced residue types, which guide backbone tracing and generate short sequence queries that are matched against user-supplied sequence pools. This addresses a major bottleneck in interpreting cryoEM maps of endogenous complexes.

papers.title: Can the Human Plastisphere Account for the Rise of Type 1 Diabetes: A Computational Molecular Mimicry Study.
papers.abstract: An increased incidence of childhood type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) has been widely documented, but its pathophysiological origins are poorly understood. The post-World War II expansion of the plastics industry in the United States and elsewhere coincides with a marked increase in T1DM incidence; however, no pathophysiological mechanism has been proposed that could justify such a temporal correlation. Here, we leverage recent advances in artificial intelligence and protein structure prediction and binding to show that molecular mimicry is a plausible pathophysiological mechanism for plastic fr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This computational study uses AI-based protein structure prediction and binding analysis to test whether molecular mimicry between human proteins and plastic-associated peptides could explain the temporal correlation between post-WWII plastic production and rising type 1 diabetes incidence. The authors propose that plastic-derived peptides may mimic self-antigens, potentially triggering autoimmune responses relevant to T1DM pathogenesis. The work is exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than experimentally validated.

papers.title: Pharmacological Mechanisms of Action and Therapeutic Basis of Qihuang Jianpi Zishen Granules in Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Study Integrating Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to clarify the material basis and mechanism by which Qihuang Jianpi Zishen granules (QHJPZSG) treat systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). UPLC-Q-TOF-MSE was used to characterize the chemical constituents of QHJPZSG and its serum-absorbed components in rats. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations were applied to screen key active compounds, potential targets, and signaling pathways, followed by in vivo validation using MRL/lpr mice and in vitro verification with primary B cells. In total, 114 constituents were identified in QHJPZSG, including
papers.summary: This study characterizes the chemical constituents of a traditional Chinese medicine formula (Qihuang Jianpi Zishen granules) and uses network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to predict its mechanisms against systemic lupus erythematosus, followed by validation in MRL/lpr mice and primary B cells. The work identifies key active compounds and signaling pathways, providing a pharmacological basis for the formula's use in SLE.

papers.title: An OGE-HPLC-ABTS-Q-TOF MS Screening of Antioxidant Components in Gushuning Tablet (GSN) With Computational Prediction of Related Biological Targets.
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) is a severe skeletal disorder that poses a major threat to public health, and oxidative stress may be one of its core pathological mechanisms. The Traditional Chinese Medicine compound preparation Gushuning Tablet (GSN) has been reported to show potential clinical benefits in OP, potentially related to the modulation of OP-associated oxidative stress. However, its antioxidant active material basis and mechanism of action remain unclear. This study aimed to establish an online gradient extraction (OGE)-high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC)-2,2'-azinobis-(3-ethylbenzthi
papers.summary: This study combines online gradient extraction HPLC with ABTS radical-scavenging detection and Q-TOF mass spectrometry to screen and identify antioxidant compounds in the traditional Chinese medicine Gushuning Tablet, a preparation used for osteoporosis. The identified antioxidant components were then subjected to computational target prediction to infer the biological pathways through which they might act against osteoporosis-related oxidative stress. The work provides a chemical and mechanistic basis for the tablet's reported clinical benefits.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics, machine learning, computational toxicology, and experimental validation reveal PFAS-associated immune-inflammatory signatures in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants increasingly implicated in respiratory disorders. However, the systems-level connections among PFAS-associated molecular perturbations, immune dysregulation, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) remain poorly understood. This study aimed to prioritize candidate links between PFAS-associated target information and COPD-related transcriptional and inflammatory signatures.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data, machine learning, computational toxicology, and experimental validation to identify molecular links between PFAS exposure and COPD. The authors prioritize candidate PFAS-associated targets that overlap with COPD-related transcriptional and immune-inflammatory signatures, suggesting mechanisms by which these environmental contaminants may contribute to respiratory disease.

papers.title: Inhibition of quorum sensing and biofilm in Pseudomonas aeruginosa by erythrinin B: Bioinformatic evidence for the LasR binding.
papers.abstract: Quorum sensing (QS)-regulated virulence factors and biofilm formation are major contributors to antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. This highlights the urgent need for novel anti-virulence strategies that can disrupt these pathways and reduce such infections. The objective of this study was to evaluate the inhibitory potential of erythrinin B against QS-regulated virulence factors and biofilm formation in P. aeruginosa PAO1. Erythrinin B significantly suppressed pyocyanin (72.27%), pyoverdin (68.22%), protease (83.08%), and elastase (62.16%) production in a dose-dependent manne
papers.summary: This study shows that erythrinin B, a natural compound, substantially reduces quorum-sensing-controlled virulence factors (pyocyanin, pyoverdin, protease, elastase) and biofilm formation in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 in a dose-dependent manner. Bioinformatic docking evidence suggests the compound binds the LasR quorum-sensing receptor, supporting an anti-virulence mechanism rather than direct killing.

papers.title: Integrated phytochemical profiling and molecular modelling of Magnolia officinalis bark-derived bioactive compounds interacting with apoptosis-associated proteins relevant to cisplatin-induced cellular injury.
papers.abstract: Cisplatin is an effective chemotherapeutic agent; however, oxidative stress and apoptosis-associated signalling contribute to both its therapeutic effects and dose-limiting toxicities. This study investigated the phytochemical composition and antioxidant properties of Magnolia officinalis bark extract and explored the predicted interactions of selected constituents with the apoptosis-associated proteins caspase-3 and BCL-2.
papers.summary: This study profiles the phytochemical composition and antioxidant activity of Magnolia officinalis bark extract, then uses molecular docking to predict how selected constituents bind to the apoptosis-related proteins caspase-3 and BCL-2. The work is exploratory and computational, offering hypotheses about how bark-derived compounds might modulate apoptotic signaling relevant to cisplatin toxicity, but without experimental validation of the predicted interactions.

papers.title: Integrative ferroptosis-related bioinformatics identifies PPARγ as a therapeutic target of ursolic acid against inflammation and pathological osteogenesis in ankylosing spondylitis.
papers.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disease characterized by persistent inflammation and aberrant new bone formation. Ferroptosis has increasingly been implicated in immune dysregulation and pathological bone remodeling; however, its molecular involvement in AS and its potential value for natural product discovery remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify ferroptosis-related molecular targets in AS, screen natural compounds targeting the key candidate, and validate their therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates ferroptosis-related bioinformatics with natural product screening to identify PPARγ as a key target in ankylosing spondylitis, then validates ursolic acid as a compound that modulates PPARγ to reduce inflammation and pathological bone formation. The work links ferroptosis biology to AS pathogenesis and proposes a natural-product therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Identification of novel compounds from Olea Europaea targeting hDus2 as potential anticancer agents: a molecular docking and molecular dynamics study.
papers.abstract: Leukemia, a type of blood cancer, ranks among the top causes of cancer-related fatalities. Human tRNA-dihydrouridine synthase 2 (hDus2) catalyzes the conversion of uridine to dihydrouridine in the tRNA and is overexpressed in cancer cells, facilitating the translational process required for cancer cell growth. Inhibition of hDus2 reduces cancer cell growth and viability while increasing apoptosis sensitivity under stress, making it an excellent cancer target. Olea Europaea is known to be abundant in flavonoids, polyphenols, vitamins, and antioxidants, and shows immense potential in providing h
papers.summary: This study uses molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to screen compounds from Olea Europaea (olive) against human tRNA-dihydrouridine synthase 2 (hDus2), an enzyme overexpressed in cancer cells that supports tumor growth. The authors identify candidate olive-derived compounds that bind hDus2 and propose them as potential anticancer agents, particularly for leukemia. The work is entirely computational and lacks experimental validation.
